text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) accused Finance Minister Marek Belka of providing a group of firms with tax breaks in violation of tax regulations.
- A group of 20 Polish and 20 Lithuanian deputies have formed a bi-national parliamentary assembly to produce common policies related to future EU integration.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSDPODARKI
- Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz arrived in Budapest on Wednesday to discuss EU integration issues and bilateral trade with Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The U.S. Monsanto chemical and pharmaceutical company plans to buy a Polish pharmaceutical plant or construct a new one, the firm's deputy president Pierre Hochulik said.
- Poland's Prime Minister Marek Belka denied reports that the ministry had written off debts owed by the Opole power plant and said it had only agreed to change the plant's repayment conditions.
- Bank Depozytowo Kredytowy (BDK) agreed to provide the listed Stalexport foreign trade firm with financial services including credits and credit consortium organisation, the companies said.

- The listed Bank Rozwoju Exportu (BRE) export development bank has bought 100 percent of shares in consulting firm Business Management & Finance (BMF). The consultancy's revenues reached $3 million in 1996.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- The shareholders of the Ciech foreign trade firm have dismissed the company's president Zdzislaw Matkiewicz. Ciech's net profit plunged by 39 percent in 1996 compared with the year before and sales declined by 8.5 percent.
- Poland will become an important link in the global economy chain and its role of a goods exporter will keep on growing, said the president of Sweden's Investor AB, Percy Barnevik.
- Nicom Consulting President Henryka Bochniarz has been reappointed chairwoman of the Polish Business Council lobbying group.
- The Gdansk refinery (RG) has increased daily output capacity to 400 tonnes from 320 tonnes following modernisation and development which cost 12 million zlotys, RG said.

- In autumn this year the U.S. Portico Development will start building an exhibition, fair and hotel complex in Gdynia, north Poland, for the World Trade Centre Gdynia (WTCG), WTCG representative Joanna Kuhn said. The project is worth up to $100 million.

- Spain's Mercasa has produced a feasibilty study of one of Europe's biggest fair centres to be located in Bedzin and Czeladz, Katowice province. The first stage of investments will cost 61 million European currency units, Mercas said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- South Korea's Daewoo has bought a 51 percent stake in the Motoprojekt construction firm worth $2.6 million and guaranteed it will invest $2 million more in development in the next three years while keeping employment at the present level. The firm changed its name to Daewoo Engineering and Construction Poland.
- Statoil will invest $100 million in new petrol station construction in Poland by the end of 1997, the company said.
PARKIET
- The Polish zloty will be devalued by up to 10 percent in 1998, Finance Minister Belka said.
- The listed Bank Slaski, controlled by ING Group, will invest $10 million in the chain's telecommunications system development, BSK's president Brunon Bartkiewicz said.
